topics.title: Cellular respiration sequence
topics.description: Glycolysis, Krebs cycle, then electron transport
topics.content: Cellular respiration converts glucose into usable energy. First, glycolysis breaks glucose into pyruvate in the cytoplasm. Then the Krebs cycle oxidizes pyruvate-derived acetyl-CoA in the mitochondrial matrix. Finally, the electron transport chain uses the resulting NADH and FADH2 to make ATP. Students often confuse the Krebs cycle with glycolysis.

questions.prompt: Where does glycolysis break glucose into pyruvate?
questions.hint: Look for the location named before mitochondria.

questions.prompt: Where is glucose broken into pyruvate during glycolysis?
What does the electron transport chain use to make ATP?

ordering.prompt: Order the main stages of cellular respiration.
ordering.explanation: Glycolysis is first, then Krebs, then electron transport.
ordering.hint: Start in the cytoplasm, then move into mitochondria.
